newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer but off highs after stocks rebound.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer but off highs after stocks rebound.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended firmer on Monday but off its session high.

Cash bond buying by investors who had sold bonds at the year-end was seen in the morning, supporting overall sentiment. But late stop-loss selling erased part of the early gains in the JGB futures market due to the Tokyo stock market's sharp rebound, traders said.
The key contract ended at 125.67, up 0.30 from Friday's close. It moved within a range between 125.47 and 125.92, with turnover at 41,081 contracts.
"Those who had refrained from buying before Friday's U.S. employment data came back to buy JGBs this morning," said a senior dealer at a long-term bank's securities unit.
After this buying from investors subsided, trading turned quiet until last-minute stop-loss selling emerged from dealers in reaction to the recovery on the stock market, he said.
But the subsequent JGB losses were limited.
Dealers cited the belief that the Nikkei stock average would start falling again unless there was a review of Japan's fiscal policy during the parliamentary session starting on January 20.
The Nikkei soared 815.14 points, or 4.71 percent, to finish at 18,118.79 on Monday. Trade was volatile as the stock index fell as low as 17,019.56 at one point.

"The stock market will be carefully watched as a clue for the direction of JGBs for the time being," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "A key point is whether the government is able to announce effective measures to support stocks when the parliamentary session starts," he said.
But some traders said that, even with the stock market gyrations, bullishness in the JGB market may linger as a result of the technical rebound after the year-end correction.

The JGB market had shrugged off fears that weak stocks may make investors sell JGBs to cover losses, they said. Unlike late last year, the drop in the Nikkei -- which shed more than 2,000 points last week -- did not trigger JGB selling.
"The key contract may try a short-term target of 126.50 in the near future," said a trust bank dealer.
Investors' cash bond buying this morning focused on the long-end of the cash JGBs, including the 190th to 192nd issues, traders said.
The yield of the 182nd 10-year JGBs stood at 2.420 percent in late Monday trade, down 0.025 from Friday's close.
